## 3. The evidence that moved it






Read against titles and journals only; no abstracts exist for 2023 in this
corpus. Every claim below is what a title and its venue will bear, and where
that is not enough the text says so.

**A ctDNA assay makes the treatment decision, in a randomized trial.**
[36863484](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36863484/) (*Ann Oncol*): the APPLE
phase 2 assigns osimertinib on plasma T790M monitoring rather than on imaging
progression. `ctdna-mrd` claims ctDNA is treatment-guiding and not only
prognostic, and this is the rare design that tests that claim directly — the
randomization is over what the assay is allowed to decide. Most ctDNA papers in
this quarter, including this month's, report association with outcome instead,
which is the other half of the thread and does not move it.

**A microbiome resistance mechanism becomes a receptor.**
[37138075](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37138075/) (*Nature*):
microbiome-related immunotherapy resistance is traced to the PD-L2–RGMb pair and
reversed by blocking it. This is the step that separates a mechanism from an
association — a named ligand and receptor, a blockade, and a reversal — and it
lands on two threads at once, since RGMb is also a non-PD-1 blockade target with
a stated route to the clinic.

**The neural arm measured in patients, with an outcome attached.**
[37138086](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37138086/) (*Nature*): glioblastoma
remodels human neural circuits and the extent of remodelling tracks survival.
Alongside it, [37169842](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37169842/) (*Nat
Cancer*) reports GAP43-dependent mitochondrial transfer from astrocytes into
glioblastoma cells. Two distinct mechanisms of tumour–neuron coupling in one
month, one of them in humans with survival as the endpoint.

**A third source of antigen that is not the host genome.**
[37198490](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37198490/) (*Nature*): microbially
derived peptides activate tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes in glioblastoma — a
tumour with almost no mutational neoantigens, which is where the
`neoantigen-vaccines` scale claim is weakest. Set against April's transposable
element convergence, the target space is being enlarged from three unrelated
directions in eight weeks: transposons, chimeric transcripts, and microbes.

**Single-cell chromatin profiling goes multifactorial as a class, not as an
instrument.** [36316484](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36316484/) reads several
histone marks simultaneously in single cells;
[36344841](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36344841/) profiles chromatin–protein
crosstalk at locus resolution in the same journal and month, and the journal
flagged the pair itself with [37138033](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37138033/).
Three more follow in June ([36536148](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36536148/),
[36536150](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36536150/),
[36593403](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36593403/)). `single-cell-3d-genome`
claims these modalities become routine inputs that downstream pipelines must
ingest; five methods in two months from independent groups is what the front edge
of that looks like, and it is also a warning that the pipelines have nothing
standard to ingest them with yet.

Section 6 shows 26 AACR 2023 abstracts landing in May — stragglers from the April
meeting, not a May event. As in April: nothing here should be read as the meeting
leading or trailing this literature, because a journal title cannot evidence that
interval in either direction.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[37195941](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37195941/) (*NEJM*): a phase 2 of
peresolimab, a **PD-1 agonist**, in rheumatoid arthritis. `next-gen-checkpoints`
claims that targets beyond PD-1 and CTLA-4 deliver a second generation of
checkpoint *blockade*. The checkpoint-axis drug that reaches a top general
journal with a phase 2 readout this month is neither beyond PD-1 nor blockade —
it runs the axis backwards, into autoimmunity. That is not a failed target; it is
the category moving sideways out from under the claim. Nothing else in the month
contradicts it — the month's other checkpoint entries
([36888930](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36888930/), CD47 with azacitidine in
higher-risk MDS) are carded as support — but the strongest clinical readout in
the axis is pointed elsewhere.

[36493337](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36493337/) (*JCO*): ctDNA is already
changing management in HPV-related oropharyngeal cancer in the absence of
guidelines to support it. This is a refutation about practice rather than
biology, and it sits in the same month as APPLE above: the assay is being acted
on faster than the evidence that acting on it helps is being generated. Both
belong to `ctdna-mrd`, and the thread is +1/−1 this month because of it.

Adjacent and carded as *supports* on `immunotherapy-resistance` rather than as a
refutation, but worth reading here:
[37205768](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37205768/) (*Sci Immunol*) reports that
PD-L1 blockade itself activates regulatory T cells in a way that underlies
therapy resistance. The therapy generating its own failure mode is support for
the resistance thread and a constraint on the blockade programme at the same time.

### (b) Method credibility

Four this month, which is why the thread reads −4 and stays in crisis.

[36930853](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36930853/) (*JCO*): response rate,
progression-free survival and overall survival are argued to have come apart from
one another. Almost every clinical readout this corpus records is reported on
response rate or progression-free survival, so this is an audit of the units the
oncology literature is denominated in.

[37024653](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37024653/) (*Nat Methods*, flagged by
the journal with [37024652](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37024652/)): in vivo
CRISPR off-target detection needed a sensitivity upgrade to see breaks it had been
missing. Published off-target profiles are therefore lower bounds set by the
assay, not counts of what the editor did — and June extends the same point to
prime editors ([37156841](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37156841/)).

[37388906](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37388906/) (*Cell Genom*): genotype
imputation reference panel accuracy is evaluated in sub-Saharan African
populations and is a function of who is in the panel. A shared resource whose
error rate depends on the ancestry of the person it is applied to, and which is
almost never quoted alongside the results built on it.

[37165242](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37165242/) (*Nature*): a draft human
pangenome reference, with [37316739](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37316739/)
in *Nat Biotechnol* the following month. The single linear reference underneath
essentially every result in this corpus is being replaced rather than extended —
and [37217946](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37217946/) shows on a bovine
super-pangenome that the graph *construction method* itself changes which
variation is representable. The foundation is not merely incomplete; the choice
of replacement is itself a variable that analyses will inherit silently.
